body:
This will not work properly once you have more than one editor group opened because then you will have more than one `div.tabs-container`. 

I suggest an alternate solution where the `accessor` provides a method to ask for the height of the editor title area. The `accessor` in this case is the `EditorPart` which can delegate this to the group in question and then the group can forward this to the title control. And I would only use the `offsetHeight` property if mutli-line tabs are enabled.

There now seems to be a weird condition under which we seem to be adding the `multi-line` class when settings change but we conditionally add and remove it in the `layout` call. Shouldn't we exclusively be setting this class only from the layout call given that this is the only place where we know that we need it when the size is little?

I would say we let the `layout` method take care and make sure it is called when this setting changes.

My suggestion was to reuse the `tab-border-bottom` helper for this case too and not introduce yet another border. Currently the `tab-border-bottom` is reserved for active tabs because the border was only used for active tabs, but to ensure we get a consistent look, we should be using the same thing for the separator as well. Otherwise we end up with an active border that is not on the exact same line as the separator border.
Done, please let me know if I've done this incorrectly.
Ah yes, I forgot about that when moving it to the `layout` method. I've removed it now, thanks.
Done, I misunderstood what you suggested earlier but hopefully it's correct now?

As you can see from the code above, the layout is scheduled `async` to prevent perf issues. As such, you return a dimension here from a time before the layout is actually applied. This is one of the issues I talked about earlier, we cannot return the height until we actually applied the CSS classes. I fear we probably have to switch to a sync layout when multi-line tabs are enabled.

Can we not simply pass the full dimensions over that we get above instead of asking the title for its height? Together with the max dimensions for the title widget I thought along the lines of:
* one parameter is the dimension of the entire group and the title widget can use it up to...
* a second parameter defines a certain maximum of size the title widget can have

Based on these 2 parameters the title widget then decides wether it goes multi-line or not.

For consistency I would suggest that `layout` returns both `height` and `width` (as a `Dimension`) and not just the one property. I would think that the `width` property can be used that is passed in because the title widget always gets as wide as what is given.

Done, it now returns a `Dimension`. It still has the problem of returning a `Dimension` before the layout call actually happens on the next scheduled frame, but once we figure out how to proceed with that, I'm sure it can be easily fit in.
Ok I can try and start working on that, what would you suggest as the maximum size the title widget can have?
Ah true, I overlooked that. I'm not very familiar with how the delegation of the layout to a new animation frame works, so I may need some assistance on the implementation here.

I would think that the maximum size is:
* `width`: the same as the entire width, aka there is no maximum
* `height`: the entire height minus the minimal height of the editor control

Ok I just pushed a very rough implementation that uses a `maxDimensions` parameter to try and remove multi-line tabs. There are problems that arise when testing, presumably due to scheduling the layout on the next frame. I'm sure it needs some fixing so let me know what you think.
@SneakyFish5 shouldn't we check on both `dimensions.available.height` and `MAX_WRAPPED_HEIGHT`? What if the available height is less than `MAX_WRAPPED_HEIGHT`?
Oh right good point, I re-added that in, thanks. Changed max amount of rows to 3 as well as requested.
